shortDescription: Manages TCL iApp services on a BIG-IP

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the iApp service. If this option is specified in the Ansible task, it takes precedence over any similar setting in the iApp Service payload that you provide in the C(parameters) field.

options.name: device_group
options.description: The device group for the iApp service. If this option is specified in the Ansible task, it takes precedence over any similar setting in the iApp Service payload that you provide in the C(parameters) field.

options.name: force
options.description: Forces the updating of an iApp service, even if the parameters to the service have not changed. This option is of particular importance if the iApp template that underlies the service has been updated in-place. This option is equivalent to re-configuring the iApp if that template has changed.

options.name: metadata
options.description: Metadata associated with the iApp service. If this option is specified in the Ansible task, it takes precedence over any similar setting in the iApp Service payload that you provide in the C(parameters) field.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the iApp service you want to deploy.

options.name: parameters
options.description: A hash of all the required template variables for the iApp template. If your parameters are stored in a file (the more common scenario) we recommend you use either the C(file) or C(template) lookups to supply the expected parameters. These parameters typically consist of the C(lists), C(tables), and C(variables) fields.

options.name: partition
options.description: Device partition to manage resources on.

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(present), ensures the iApp service is created and running. When C(absent), ensures the iApp service has been removed.

options.name: strict_updates
options.description: Indicates whether the application service is tied to the template, so when the template is updated, the application service changes to reflect the updates. When C(true), disallows any updates to the resources that the iApp service has created, if they are not updated directly through the iApp. When C(false), allows updates outside of the iApp. If this option is specified in the Ansible task, it takes precedence over any similar setting in the iApp Service payload that you provide in the C(parame

options.name: template
options.description: The iApp template from which to instantiate a new service. This template must exist on your BIG-IP before you can successfully create a service. When creating a new service, this parameter is required.

options.name: traffic_group
options.description: The traffic group for the iApp service. When creating a new service, if this value is not specified, the default of C(/Common/traffic-group-1) is used. If this option is specified in the Ansible task, it takes precedence over any similar setting in the iApp Service payload that you provide in the C(parameters) field.
